definitions.definition: The science (vidyā) taught in this text solely for the sake of rājayoga (1.2); its practices (postures, retentions, mudrās, inner-sound attention) run up to the fruit of rājayoga (1.67); it is a shelter and support for the afflicted and for those devoted to yoga (1.10), to be kept secret (1.11); without rājayoga it does not succeed, nor rājayoga without it (2.76); its practitioners who do not know rājayoga are said to labour without fruit (4.79).

The aim for which haṭha is taught (1.2); the text lists it as one of the words for samādhi (4.3-4) and says that on the mind becoming one 'this is called rājayoga' (4.77); all means of haṭha and laya are for its accomplishment (4.103).
A state of the mind named among the synonyms of samādhi (4.3); the text says duality is not perceived through the mind's becoming unmanī (4.61) and the body becomes like wood in it (4.106).
One of the words the text gives for the same state as rājayoga and samādhi (4.4).

The natural state (sahajāvasthā): it arises of itself for the yogin who has given up all action and in whom awareness of śakti has arisen (4.11), is hard to gain without the true guru's compassion (4.9), and 'sahajā' is one of the words for samādhi (4.4).

The inner sound heard in the practice of nādānusandhāna (4.67-68, 4.82-86); the text says whatever is heard as nāda is śakti itself (4.102), that laya rests on nāda (4.29) and that the soundless is the supreme Brahman (4.101).

The middle channel: its synonyms are śūnyapadavī, brahmarandhra, mahāpatha, śmaśāna, śāmbhavī and madhyamārga (3.4); the text calls it the only fruitful one of 72,000 channel-doors (4.18) and the devourer of Time (4.17).

Called the support of all yoga-tantras (3.1); the text says that when she wakes by the guru's grace all lotuses and knots are pierced (3.2); given seven synonyms (3.104), described as sleeping over the door of Brahman (3.106-107).

In the HYP: the union (sāmya) of the self and the mind as salt is with water (4.5), the state in which breath is exhausted and mind dissolved, of 'sameness of taste' (4.6), the oneness of jīvātman and paramātman with all resolves destroyed (4.7); the text gives a long list of synonyms (4.3-4).

notes: Sense-specific id: the existing trm:samadhi carries only an Advaita (Gauḍapāda) definition.

definitions.definition: In the HYP: the dissolution of mind and breath together (4.15, 4.23), described as 'forgetting of objects' because latent impressions do not rise again (4.34); it is 'lord of the breath' and rests on nāda (4.29).

notes: Sense-specific id: the existing trm:laya has Advaita (Kārikā) definitions.

definitions.definition: In the HYP the 'void' is the space in which the breath dissolves (4.10), which the mind enters (4.12), the 'great void' of the third stage (4.74) and the path of the void (śūnyapadavī) that names suṣumnā (3.4).

notes: Sense-specific id: the existing trm:sunya is the Madhyamaka 'empty of own-nature'.

definitions.definition: In the HYP a 'lock' (uḍḍīyāna, mūlabandha, jālandhara; also mahābandha); summary only, no method recorded.

notes: Sense-specific id: the existing cpt:bandha and trm:bandha are Jain 'bondage'. Restricted practice group.
